title: Use Privacy in Data-Driven Systems: Theory and Experiments with Machine Learnt Programs
reasoning: The paper includes a significant component regarding ethical and normative judgments in privacy. It introduces a 'normative judgment oracle' to decide if the use of proxies for protected information (such as religion or health status) is appropriate. Furthermore, it specifically evaluates how religious affiliation can be inferred through proxies in machine learning models and treats this as a case study for normative privacy violations.
